title: `vmap` of `clamp` raises if only `max` is batched and `min` and the operand are scalars

found: https://github.com/jax-ml/jax/issues/5325 (closed 2021): `vmap` of `lax.clamp` raised with all three arguments batched. That case works now, this one was not part of it.

description: `vmap` of `lax.clamp` over `max` alone raises a `TypeError` if `min` and the operand are scalars.
It works if `min` is batched, with or without `max`, and if the operand is not a scalar.
expected: `lax.clamp` accepts bounds that are scalars or have the shape of the operand,
so `clamp(min, x, max)` is defined for each entry of a batched `max`.
`vmap` should return the same as a loop over the entries, as it does when `min` is batched.
reproducer: lo, x, hi = jnp.array(0.0), jnp.array(1.0), jnp.array(3.0)
# Clamping x = 1 between lo = 0 and each upper bound.
print(jnp.stack([lax.clamp(lo, x, h) for h in bounds]))
# vmap works over the lower bound, and over both bounds.
print(jax.vmap(lambda l, h: lax.clamp(l, x, h))(bounds, bounds + 1))
# vmap over the upper bound alone raises.
# actual:  TypeError: clamp requires max.shape == operand.shape or max.shape == (), got max.shape=(3,), operand.shape=().
# It works if x is not a scalar.
cause: Under `vmap`, a batched scalar bound has shape `(size,)`,
so `_clamp_batch_rule` has to broadcast an unbatched scalar operand to that shape.
Its general case does so only for a batched `min`:
If only `max` is batched, the operand stays a scalar, and `clamp_p.bind` rejects `max` of shape `(size,)`.
lean: `Jax.Lax.clampBatch` transcribes the rule on arrays of any shape,
and `Jax.Lax.clampBatch_not_correct` shows that it raises for a batch of size 1.
`scripts/shapes.py` checks the model against `_clamp_batch_rule` on 1500 combinations of shapes and batch axes
(result shape, batch axis and raised cases):
this is the only combination of batched arguments that raises.
